tips.content: Dynamic toolpaths utilize as much of the tool's flute length as possible while minimizing tool burial. This enables rapid and efficient material removal while extending tool life.
2D high speed dynamic milling toolpaths provide three key benefits: tool burial avoidance, minimum heat buildup, and better chip evacuation.
Dynamic Mill with Stay Inside strategy machines pockets using one or more chains to drive the toolpath. Material is removed from inside to outside in a highly efficient manner.

Dynamic Mill Rest Material strategy targets material left from previous operations. Only unmachined areas are processed, making it ideal when roughing tools leave material in corners or narrow part areas.
Dynamic Mill From Outside strategy machines open pocket shapes or standing core shapes. The tool moves freely outside the stock boundary and works from outside toward the inner boundary.

Dynamic Contour mills material off walls supporting closed or open chains. The tool motion converts to dynamic in areas where the tool would bind or encounter too much material. Use on walls or contours with small radii.
Micro lift options allow the tool to rise above the floor during non-cutting moves. Benefits include chip clearing and avoiding excess tool heat. The feedrate is controllable for the back move.
Use entry feeds and speeds to avoid placing too much load on the tool upon entry. Set a short dwell interval after entry to allow the spindle to reach necessary speed before material removal.
Contour wall parameters provide input for remaining stock and previous tool information. These values help Mastercam calculate the most efficient material removal strategy when machining part walls.
Use Analyze > Volume/Area > 2D Area on selected chains if the toolpath is not being created as expected. The cause will often be an incorrect assumption about the enclosed 2D area of geometry.
Avoidance regions allow you to add geometry to avoid without modifying original part geometry. Simply sketch a rectangle to represent a clamp, add it to the operation's chains, and regenerate.
Containment regions are areas that the tool cannot move outside of. The toolpath is constrained inside the containment boundary while still avoiding avoidance regions.
Air regions define areas with no material. By partially chaining a line segment as an Air region, Mastercam knows there is no material there, allowing the tool to travel through when machining.
Use micro lift distance to raise the tool above the floor when making connecting moves. The lift creates time where heat is not being added to the tool or part, extending tool life.
Profile entry method with Z clearance and plunge angle parameters provides controlled entry into the material for Dynamic Mill operations.

Dynamic Mill can cut material at full depth using as much of the tool's flute length as necessary. Depth cuts are available for pocket depths and materials that prevent full-depth single-pass machining.
Dynamic Mill with Stay Inside strategy can remove pocket material in less than half the time of a standard Pocket operation while achieving similar surface finish on walls.
For Dynamic Mill Rest operations, deselect 'Optimize cut order within pocket' and set % of tool diameter to 500% to maximize engagement with remaining material.
Tool Manager's new TOOLDB database format is faster and more reliable than older formats. Its non-proprietary format allows tooling manufacturers to keep you updated with recent tooling components.
Work in stand-alone Tool Manager without Mastercam open to organize tool libraries. This increases computer performance and reserves the licensed Mastercam seat for someone else.
Copy tools, holders, and assemblies between TOOLDB libraries by opening different libraries in separate Tool Manager instances and using drag-and-drop between them.
Set up tool libraries using stand-alone Tool Manager, then use those libraries in Mastercam for specific jobs, parts, and machines. Libraries can be part of a job kit that travels with the part.
The default unit setting in Tool Manager is read from Mastercam's System Configuration. Tool Manager remains in metric/inch state until manually changed, even across multiple sessions.
You can have both inch and metric tooling components in the same TOOLDB library file.
Cut parameters stored in Tool Manager integrate manufacturer's cutting recommendations. Access these from Mastercam when creating or editing tools with the Tool Wizard.
When creating a new WCS: XY plane maps to the plane of the view, the origin becomes your new (0,0,0) point, and the plane becomes the Top plane in the new working coordinate system.
Gviews, Cplanes, and Tplanes are all measured relative to the WCS and its origin. Select a new WCS much less often than views and planes, and only for specific machining purposes.
Construction plane (Cplane) is where geometry is created. You can look at your part in Isometric Gview while drawing geometry in the Front Cplane - they do not have to match.
Tool plane (Tplane) is typically normal to the tool axis. Unless Tplane is parallel to the default XY plane, selecting a Tplane typically results in A- and/or B-axis codes when posting.
To post A- and B-axis code results, your machine definition must be configured with proper rotary axis components and your post must be properly configured for rotary output.
Change the WCS to machine a part lying flat instead of rotating the tool. Rotate the coordinate system parallel with the desired face to machine on a 3-axis mill without rotary capability.
Machine two parts on different fixtures using one setup by creating separate WCS planes for each fixture position, then applying appropriate planes to each toolpath group.
Update previously created toolpaths when part position changes by creating new WCS planes and reassigning them to existing operations rather than recreating toolpaths from scratch.
Use Renishaw Productivity+ for part setup, tool height settings, tool breakage checking, and inspection/reporting of basic geometric features (points, lines, planes, circles, web and pocket sizes).
Productivity+ can measure machined areas and dynamically set offsets to remachine features that are undersized. It also detects oversized features that cannot be remachined and can stop the machine.
Productivity+ supports only Renishaw probes and will not probe complex free flowing surfaces. Current version does not support continuous 4- or 5-axis motion for probing.
Probing operations require two-stage posting: standard Mastercam post creates initial output, then Renishaw machine file (.RenMF) incorporates probe-specific instructions.
Calibrate your probe with your controller AND with Productivity+ software before attempting to use it in production. Create a calibration cycle from Probe Calibration button in Probing Dialog.
In one probe operation, you can establish tool offsets for all tools in the tool magazine. Create tool setting cycle for each tool including tool length and diameter measurements.
Use tool breakage detection during processing to determine aberrations in tool diameter and length. If breakage is detected, an error is automatically output to the control.
Probing can update WCS by measuring part position. Probe a point at part top to redefine Z coordinate, then probe pocket sides to establish XY center position.
WCS planes available for probing updates are populated from Mastercam's Plane Manager. Work offset numbers assigned in Plane Manager are automatically used when the plane is changed.
Use logic statements in probe operations to check for out-of-tolerance measurements. Program Productivity+ to modify tool offsets and remachine, or stop for features that cannot be repaired.
When creating solids in Mastercam, all operations appear in the solids history tree where you can edit, move, delete, and suppress operations to modify the model.
Model Prep functions let you modify solid models lacking a history tree. Mastercam can identify individual geometry elements and features for modification using Push-Pull, Move, and Split Solid Face.
Use Add boss operation to create extrusions as new material on the part. This adds geometry rather than creating a separate solid body.
Draft angle settings are remembered during your Mastercam session. Turn on Draft in the Advanced tab with a specified angle (e.g., 5 degrees) to apply to extrusions automatically.
Use Shading Translucency Toggle to see geometry hidden under existing solid features. This helps when chaining wireframe that is embedded in or under solid bodies.
Cut body operation is opposite of Add boss - it removes material from the part. Use Through all option with Cut body to cut completely through the solid regardless of depth.
Dynamic Mill requires at least one Machining region defined (closed or open chain). Remaining geometry can be Avoidance region, Containment region, or Air region.
Dynamic Contour does not require a closed chain to calculate a toolpath. All geometry selected will be cut by the tool motion, making it flexible for wall machining.
Entry methods for Dynamic Mill range from simple helix to medial path with trochoidal motion to selected open chain. Choose based on material, tool, and part geometry.
Data in Tool Manager is automatically saved as you work, avoiding possible work loss and eliminating the need for manual backups during tool library editing.

Tool Manager Database Explorer accesses content in TOOLDB files. Right-click items to expand/collapse. Double-click Cutting Tools, Tool Assemblies, Holders, Materials, or Cut Parameters to work with them.
Tool Assemblies may contain one tool and one or more holder components. Use the Assembly Tree to navigate individual assembly items and create complete tool setups.
Display relative to WCS option shows names of tool and construction planes relative to the WCS rather than absolute names, making it easier to understand plane relationships.
XY plane of your toolpath is parallel to the selected view. The origin of the selected view determines the zero point of your part program. Plan WCS carefully for proper output.
Probe operation is stored in Toolpaths Manager like other operations. The operation is a snapshot of your model at creation time - updating the part model will not mark a probe operation dirty.
You can probe points, lines, circles/arcs, planes, 2D corners, 3D corners, webs, and pockets. Select probe method from Probing Dialog toolbar and enter required data for inspection.
Use the visual ruler when extruding to enter distances by moving mouse. Zoom in with mouse wheel to see smaller increments. Values snap to ruler increments when mouse is over the ruler.
Backplot Info tab shows total runtime for each operation. Use this to compare Dynamic Mill vs standard Pocket operations and quantify efficiency improvements.
Dynamic Mill operations can achieve similar wall finish to Pocket with finish pass, but in significantly less time. Even without optimization, Dynamic shows substantial productivity improvements.
Use the Search window in Tool Manager to find components matching criteria. Save searches as Favorites for reuse and view recent searches for quick access.

Create assemblies by dragging and dropping components into Assembly Tree, or work directly in the graphics window to edit. Properties Grid allows editing of assembly and individual component parameters.
Only display selected toolpaths button in Toolpaths Manager helps reduce visual clutter when multiple operations exist. Toggle toolpath display with T key.
Set linking parameters with Retract, Feed plane, Top of stock, and Depth values. Use Incremental setting for most parameters except Top of stock which is typically Absolute.
Add draft to solids before adding fillets. Draft operation works on flat faces; filleted edges may prevent proper draft application. Sequence solid operations for best results.
Shell operation hollows out a solid with specified wall thickness. Select faces to remain open (removed) during shelling. Useful for creating enclosures and housings.
Revolve creates solids by rotating a profile around an axis. Define the profile geometry and select the axis of revolution. Use for cylindrical or axisymmetric parts.
Sweep creates solids by sweeping a profile along a path. The profile follows the path orientation. Use for complex shapes that follow a curve or trajectory.
Boolean operations combine solids: Add (union) joins solids, Remove (subtract) cuts one solid from another, Common (intersect) keeps only overlapping volume.
Split Solid Face in Model Prep separates a solid into multiple bodies at a specified face. Use to separate features for individual machining or modification.
Push-Pull in Model Prep modifies face positions on brick solids. Select a face and drag or enter a distance to move it, automatically adjusting connected geometry.
Standard Pocket with 50% stepover equals 8mm stepover distance for 16mm tool. Compare this engagement to Dynamic Mill's full-depth engagement for efficiency analysis.
Ramp entry with specified parameters (angle, minimum ramp length, XY clearance) provides controlled material entry for Pocket operations. Enable with checkbox on Entry Motion page.
Depth cuts with specified max rough step break deep pockets into multiple Z-level passes. Essential for materials that cannot be machined at full depth in single pass.
Access cut parameters directly from Mastercam during toolpath creation. When selecting a tool, the associated cut parameters (speeds, feeds) are loaded from the Tool Manager database.
Create tools and holders directly from toolpath dialog. Launch Tool Wizard to define new tool geometry and parameters without leaving the toolpath creation workflow.
Enter 0 for tool offset index to match it to the tool change ID for any value greater than 9. Simplifies tool setting setup for large tool magazines.
Create new WCS planes using solid face selection. Select a flat face on the solid and Mastercam creates a plane aligned with that face for toolpath orientation.
When updating toolpaths to new WCS planes, select the operation's Planes page and choose new WCS. Regenerate the operation to apply the new coordinate system.
Area Mill toolpath with Rest Mill strategy is the predecessor to Dynamic Mill Rest. Both target leftover material, but Dynamic Mill uses modern efficient motion patterns.
Dynamic Mill with Rest Mill strategy improves on Area Mill with Rest Mill by avoiding tool burial while taking full depth of cut. Choose Dynamic for efficiency in corner cleanup.
Dynamic Mill From Outside strategy starts toolpath outside the selected boundary and works inward. Tool is allowed to move freely outside the Machining region boundary.
Dynamic Contour uses Entry chain option for controlled material entry. Select an open chain at the part edge for the tool to follow before engaging the contour.
Standard Contour toolpath with ramping entry can compare to Dynamic Contour. Dynamic version prevents tool binding in tight radii and converts motion dynamically as needed.
Use Align Vertical Wall in Model Prep to adjust wall angle on imported solids. Specify the target angle (e.g., 90 degrees) to make walls perpendicular to the base.
Expand Wall Opening in Model Prep increases hole or pocket size on brick solids. Select the faces defining the opening and specify new dimensions or offset amount.
Increase Wall Height in Model Prep extends vertical faces of brick solids. Select the top face and specify additional height without recreating the solid from scratch.
Create counterbores on imported solids using Hole modification in Model Prep. Select existing hole and add counterbore geometry without rebuilding the solid model.
Multi-editing allows selecting multiple tools in Tool Manager and editing common properties for all selected items simultaneously via Properties Grid. Massive time saver for bulk changes.
Productivity+ can generate reports of probing results. Configure reporting options to output measurement data, deviations, and pass/fail status for quality documentation.
Mastercam YouTube channel (youtube.com/user/MastercamTechDocs) contains video tutorials referenced in documentation. Use for visual learning of Dynamic Milling and other features.
Mill and Lathe products provide both classic Tool Manager (integrated) and new stand-alone Tool Manager. Use classic for quick in-toolpath tool selection; stand-alone for library management.

procedures.title: Create Dynamic Mill Toolpath (Stay Inside Strategy)
steps: Select Toolpaths > 2D High Speed > Dynamic Mill from menu
Click OK if prompted for new NC file name
In Chain Options, click Select under Machining regions
Chain the boundary geometry counterclockwise
Click OK to close Chaining dialog
Add Avoidance regions if needed for islands or fixtures
Verify Machining region strategy is set to Stay inside
Click OK to close Chain Options
Select Tool page and choose appropriate end mill
Set Cut Parameters including micro lift distance
Select Entry Motion and choose entry method (Profile, Helix, etc.)
Set Linking Parameters with appropriate depths
Click OK to generate toolpath

procedures.title: Create Dynamic Mill Toolpath (Rest Mill Strategy)
steps: Select Toolpaths > 2D High Speed > Dynamic Mill
Chain Machining regions (outer boundary)
Chain Avoidance regions (islands)
Close chaining dialogs
Select smaller tool than previous operation
On Cut Parameters page, set % of tool diameter (e.g., 500%)
Deselect 'Optimize cut order within pocket'
Go to Rest Material page and enable Rest material checkbox
Specify previous tool diameter or select from operations
Set Entry Motion method
Configure Linking Parameters
Click OK to generate rest mill toolpath

procedures.title: Create Dynamic Contour Toolpath
steps: Select Toolpaths > 2D High Speed > Dynamic Contour
Select geometry chains (can be open or closed)
Click OK in Chain Options
Select appropriate tool (bullnose recommended for walls)
Set Cut Parameters for wall machining
Configure Entry Motion (Entry chain for edge approach)
Set Linking Parameters with retract and depth values
Click OK to generate dynamic contour

procedures.title: Add Avoidance/Containment/Air Regions to Dynamic Toolpath
steps: Click Geometry under the operation in Toolpaths Manager
In Chain Options, click Select under desired region type
For Avoidance: chain geometry to avoid (islands, fixtures)
For Containment: chain boundary to constrain tool
For Air: use Partial chaining for open chain at air/no-material areas
Click OK in Chaining dialog
Click OK in Chain Options
Click Regenerate all dirty operations

procedures.title: Create Tool Library in Stand-Alone Tool Manager
prerequisites: Tool Manager launched from Start menu
steps: Open Tool Manager from Windows Start > Mastercam folder
Click File tab > Options > General > set Units to Metric/Inch as needed
Click OK to save settings
To create new library: File > New > enter library name
To copy existing: Open source library, File > Save As new name
Double-click Cutting Tools in Database Explorer to view tools
Add new tools: right-click > New Tool > select tool type
Fill tool geometry and parameters in Properties Grid
Create holders similarly under Holders
Create assemblies by dragging tools and holders to Assembly Tree

procedures.title: Configure Work Coordinate System (WCS)
steps: Click Planes in Status Bar > Named planes > Plane List
Create new plane or select existing plane
To create from face: select solid face as plane basis
To create manually: specify origin and orientation
Set as WCS: click WCS in Status Bar > select plane name
Verify Gview shows updated coordinate orientation
In toolpath, go to Planes (WCS) page
Click Select WCS plane button
Choose appropriate plane from list
Enable 'Display relative to WCS' for clarity

procedures.title: Set Up Renishaw Probing
steps: Select Toolpaths > Probe from menu
In Select probe dialog, click Create for new probe setup
Enter Probe name matching machine/installation
Set Tool change ID to probe's tool slot number
Select Probe module from dropdown matching hardware
Select Stylus type attached to probe module
Click OK to save to database (.RenPD)
Run probe calibration cycle before production use
Create probe operations for part setup, tool setting, or inspection
Post with Renishaw-enabled post processor

procedures.title: Create Probing Cycle for Part Setup
steps: Select Toolpaths > Probe
Probing Dialog opens with configured probe
Select measurement type: Point, Circle, Pocket, etc.
Select geometry or enter measurement parameters
Add Machine Update cycle after measurement
Choose update type: WCS Update, Tool Lengths, etc.
Select target WCS plane from Plane Manager list
Configure X, Y, Z coordinate updates as needed
Add logic statements for tolerance checking if required
Click OK to create probe operation
Post with two-stage process (MP post + RenMF)

procedures.title: Create Solid Model Using Extrude
steps: Create 2D profile geometry (rectangle, circle, or complex shape)
Select Solids > Extrude from menu
Chaining dialog opens - select profile geometry
Click OK in Chaining dialog
Use function panel to set extrusion direction (Reverse All if needed)
Set extrude distance using number entry or visual ruler
For adding material: select Add boss operation
For cutting material: select Cut body operation
Optional: click Advanced tab to add Draft angle
Click OK to finalize extrude operation
Operation appears in Solids history tree

procedures.title: Modify Imported Solid Using Model Prep
steps: Open imported solid file in Mastercam
Select Solids > Model Prep from menu
Choose modification type: Push-Pull, Split Face, etc.
For Push-Pull: select face to move, drag or enter distance
For Split: select face to split solid bodies
For Align Vertical: select wall faces, specify angle (90 deg)
For Expand Opening: select hole/pocket faces, specify new size
For Wall Height: select top face, specify height increase
Mastercam adjusts connected geometry automatically
Verify results and repeat for additional modifications

procedures.title: Compare Dynamic Mill vs Standard Pocket Performance
prerequisites: Both toolpaths created on same geometry
steps: Create Dynamic Mill toolpath with full-depth parameters
Create Pocket toolpath on same geometry with depth cuts
Select first operation in Toolpaths Manager
Click Backplot selected operations
Click Expand and select Info tab
Note total runtime displayed
Close backplot and select second operation
Repeat backplot and record runtime
Compare cycle times - Dynamic typically 50%+ faster
Verify surface finish quality if needed

procedures.title: Copy Tools Between Tool Libraries
steps: Open first Tool Manager instance
Load source TOOLDB library
Open second Tool Manager instance (new window)
Load destination TOOLDB library
In source: navigate to tools to copy
Select tools in document datagrid (Ctrl+click for multiple)
Drag selected tools to destination Tool Manager window
Drop on Cutting Tools in Database Explorer
Tools are copied with all properties
Repeat for holders and assemblies as needed

procedures.title: Update Toolpath for New Fixture Position
steps: Create new WCS plane for new fixture position
Set origin and orientation to match fixture
In Toolpaths Manager, click Parameters under operation
Navigate to Planes (WCS) page
Click Select WCS plane button
Choose new fixture plane from list
Click OK to accept changes
Regenerate dirty operations
Verify toolpath position in graphics window
Post process with updated coordinate output

procedures.title: Create Tool Assembly with Holder
steps: Double-click Tool Assemblies in Database Explorer
Assembly Tree appears below Database Explorer
Right-click in Assembly Tree > New Assembly
Enter assembly name
Drag cutting tool from Cutting Tools document to assembly
Drag holder from Holders document to assembly
Use Properties Grid to adjust offset/orientation
Graphics window shows assembled tool
Verify reach and clearance visually
Save assembly - auto-saved to TOOLDB

procedures.title: Create Probing Remachine Cycle
steps: Create probe operation for feature measurement
Select feature type (circle, pocket, etc.)
Define nominal dimensions and tolerances
Add Logic statement after inspection
Configure IF condition for undersized feature
Add tool offset update action (diameter, wear)
Add remachine toolpath reference
Configure ELSE for oversized (cannot remachine)
Add stop/error action for out-of-spec oversized
Close logic statement
Post and verify cycle sequence

procedures.title: Configure Entry Motion for Dynamic Mill
steps: Navigate to Entry Motion page in toolpath dialog
Select Entry method from dropdown: Helix, Profile, or Custom chain
For Helix: set minimum radius, plunge angle, Z clearance
For Profile: set Z clearance and plunge angle
For Custom chain: click Select, chain open entry geometry
Set Entry speed/feed percentages if different from cut
Set Dwell interval after entry (allows spindle stabilization)
Click OK to apply entry settings
Backplot to verify entry motion path

procedures.title: Add Boolean Operations to Solid Model
prerequisites: Two or more solid bodies exist
steps: Select Solids > Boolean from menu
Choose operation type: Add, Remove, or Common
For Add (union): select bodies to join together
For Remove (subtract): select target, then tool body
For Common (intersect): select bodies to intersect
Preview shows result before accepting
Click OK to perform boolean operation
Result is single solid body
Operation recorded in history tree for editing

procedures.title: Shell Solid Model
steps: Select Solids > Shell from menu
Enter wall thickness value
Select faces to remain open (removed during shelling)
Typically select top face for box/enclosure shapes
Preview shows hollow result
Adjust thickness if walls appear too thin/thick
Click OK to create shelled solid
Interior is hollowed with uniform wall thickness

procedures.title: Post Process with Probe Operations
steps: Select operations to post in Toolpaths Manager
Click Post selected operations
In Post Processing dialog, select Renishaw-enabled post
Click OK - Probing Post Tool dialog appears
Select appropriate RenMF file for your machine
Configure probing output options
Click OK to generate NC code
NC file includes both machining and probing code
Verify probing sequences in code output

procedures.title: Machine Multiple Fixtures with Single Setup
steps: Open Plane Manager from Status Bar
Create WCS plane for first fixture position
Set origin at fixture datum, orientation to match fixture
Create second WCS plane for second fixture position
Create toolpaths for first part using first WCS
Transform or copy toolpaths for second fixture
Assign second WCS to copied toolpaths
Work offsets (G54, G55, etc.) assigned via Plane Manager
Post process all operations
NC code includes work offset changes between fixtures

procedures.title: Add Fillet and Chamfer to Solid Model
prerequisites: Solid model with edges to blend
steps: For Fillet: Select Solids > Fillet
Select edges to fillet (can select multiple)
Enter fillet radius
Preview shows blended result
For Chamfer: Select Solids > Chamfer
Choose chamfer type: Distance, Distance-Angle, etc.
Select edges to chamfer
Enter chamfer values
Click OK to apply
Note: Apply draft before fillets for best results

procedures.title: Troubleshoot Unexpected Toolpath Results
prerequisites: Toolpath created but not as expected
steps: Check chaining direction using Analyze > Volume/Area > 2D Area
Verify enclosed 2D area matches expectations
Check region assignments (Machining, Avoidance, Containment)
Verify Machining region strategy (Stay Inside, From Outside, Rest)
Check for overlapping or intersecting chains
Verify tool diameter vs geometry clearances
Check stock-to-leave values
Regenerate operation after changes
Use Backplot to visualize actual tool motion
Compare with similar working toolpath if available

procedures.title: Configure Micro Lift for Dynamic Toolpath
prerequisites: Dynamic Mill or Dynamic Contour parameters open
steps: Navigate to Cut Parameters page
Locate Micro lift section
Enable micro lift checkbox
Set lift distance (amount tool raises above floor)
Set back feedrate percentage for retract moves
Benefits: chip clearing, reduced tool heat
Adjust based on material and chip characteristics
Backplot to verify lift motion in toolpath

procedures.title: Create Tool Breakage Detection Cycle
steps: Create probe operation from Toolpaths menu
Select Tool Setting from menu in Probing Dialog
Choose Broken Tool Detection from fly-out
Select tool setter type matching your hardware
Enter Tool change ID number
Enter tool offset index (0 to match ID if >9)
Configure measurement type and parameters
Add to toolpath sequence after cutting operations
If breakage detected, error outputs to control
Program stops for operator intervention

procedures.title: Access Cut Parameters from Tool Library
steps: In toolpath dialog, select Tool page
Click Select library tool button
Navigate to tool with cut parameters
Select tool and click OK
Cut parameters (speeds/feeds) auto-populate
Values based on material and operation type
Adjust parameters if needed for specific application
To view/edit cut parameters: open Tool Manager
Double-click Cut Parameters in Database Explorer

procedures.title: Create Counterbore on Imported Solid
steps: Select Solids > Model Prep > Hole modification
Select existing hole face
Choose Add counterbore option
Enter counterbore diameter (larger than hole)
Enter counterbore depth
Preview shows counterbore feature
Click OK to create counterbore
Counterbore added without rebuilding model

procedures.title: Multi-Edit Tools in Tool Manager
steps: Open Tools document in Tool Manager
Select first tool to edit
Ctrl+click to add additional tools to selection
Or Shift+click for range selection
Properties Grid shows common properties
Edit shared property (e.g., coolant type)
Change applies to ALL selected tools
Different values show as blank - edit to set same value
Significant time savings for bulk updates

procedures.title: Verify Dynamic Mill Cycle Time Savings
prerequisites: Dynamic Mill and Pocket operations on same geometry
steps: Select Dynamic Mill operation
Click Backplot selected operations
Click Play to run simulation
Click Expand > Info tab
Record total runtime
Close backplot
Select Pocket operation
Repeat backplot and record runtime
Calculate percentage savings
Document for process improvement tracking

parameter_guidance.guidance: Set 0.5-2mm above floor to clear chips and reduce tool heat during non-cutting moves. Higher values for sticky materials.
parameter_guidance.when_to_use: Dynamic Mill and Dynamic Contour operations

parameter_guidance.guidance: Helix for open areas with room to spiral. Profile for controlled plunge with clearance. Custom chain when entry point must be at specific location (edge, pre-drilled hole).
parameter_guidance.when_to_use: All Dynamic toolpaths requiring material entry

parameter_guidance.guidance: For Dynamic Mill Rest, use 400-500% to maximize engagement with remaining material. Standard operations typically 25-75% depending on material.
Stay Inside: standard pockets. From Outside: facing with island avoidance, open shapes. Rest Material: leftover cleanup from larger tools.
Set 0.5-2 seconds after entry to allow spindle to reach target RPM before material engagement. Critical for high-speed spindles.
Enter remaining stock amount from previous operations. Mastercam uses this to calculate efficient wall machining strategy.
Dynamic toolpaths use full flute length. Ensure flute length exceeds required depth of cut. Insufficient flute length causes tool burial.
For standard Pocket: enable when material/tool cannot handle full-depth cutting. Dynamic Mill typically uses full depth without depth cuts.
Disable for Rest Mill operations to ensure all remaining material is addressed. Enable for standard operations to minimize rapid movements.
Set micro lift retract feedrate as percentage of cut feedrate. 100-200% typical. Higher reduces non-cutting time.
parameter_guidance.when_to_use: Dynamic operations with micro lift enabled

parameter_guidance.guidance: 1-3 degrees typical for controlled material entry. Lower angles reduce entry forces but increase entry time.
Height above material where controlled entry begins. 0.5-2mm typical. Must clear chips and provide safe transition.
Safe Z for rapid moves between cuts. Set above all obstructions including clamps and fixtures. Use Incremental from Top of Stock typically.
Height where tool switches from rapid to feed. Typically 2-5mm above Top of Stock. Set Incremental.
Set to 0 to auto-match Tool Change ID when ID is greater than 9. Simplifies setup for large tool magazines.
2-5 degrees typical for injection molds. Apply before fillets as draft works on flat faces.
parameter_guidance.when_to_use: Solid extrude operations for moldable parts

parameter_guidance.guidance: Ensure minimum wall thickness is machinable (typically >0.5mm for milling). Consider part function and material strength.
Set 0.5-1mm for roughing operations that will be followed by finishing. Set 0 for final operations.
Typically 0 for pockets. Non-zero if floor will be re-machined by separate finishing operation.
Default 0.0254mm (0.001 inch). Increase if geometry has small gaps. Decrease for precision work.
Set to allow tool to spiral without hitting walls. Typically 25-50% of tool diameter plus allowance.
Align with fixture datum or part zero. All toolpath coordinates are relative to this point.
Set normal to tool axis direction. Non-default Tplane triggers rotary axis output in posted code.
Match stylus in software to physical stylus on machine. Incorrect selection causes measurement errors.
Select exact Renishaw module model installed on machine. Different modules have different specifications.
Select workpiece material when accessing cut parameters. Speeds/feeds adjust based on material selection.
Set Z offset where holder connects to tool. Verify in graphics window for proper assembly visualization.
50% typical for standard pocketing. Dynamic Mill calculates engagement automatically for optimal performance.
1 pass typical for wall finish. Additional passes for better surface finish at cost of cycle time.
2-5 degrees for controlled ramp entry into pockets. Lower angles = less axial force but longer entry.
Set based on tool capability and material. Typically 1-3mm for steels with standard end mills.
Enable to show plane names relative to current WCS instead of absolute names. Improves clarity when working with multiple coordinate systems.
Set acceptance tolerance for probed measurements. Features outside tolerance trigger logic actions (remachine or stop).
1-999 available for tool numbers. Plan numbering scheme for tool magazine organization.
Assign unique holder numbers for tool magazine management. Used with tool assemblies.
Use partial chaining for air regions. Open chain indicates no material boundary allowing tool to pass through.
parameter_guidance.when_to_use: Dynamic Mill with air entry required

parameter_guidance.guidance: Chain closed boundary that tool must stay within. Useful for limiting machining to specific part area.
Chain geometry to avoid (islands, fixtures). Toolpath routes around these areas automatically.
Add (union) joins solids. Remove (subtract) cuts tool from target. Common (intersect) keeps only overlap.
Use Reverse All to flip extrusion direction. Direction determines which side material is added/removed.
Enable to cut completely through solid regardless of specified depth. Useful for holes and slots.

high_speed_machining.content: Dynamic toolpaths minimize tool burial by using full flute length engagement. Tool moves through material rather than plunging into it.
Micro lift during non-cutting moves prevents heat accumulation in tool and workpiece. Essential for high-speed operations.
Entry dwell allows spindle to reach programmed RPM before cutting engagement. Prevents tool loading during spindle acceleration.
Dynamic Mill achieves 50%+ cycle time reduction compared to standard Pocket operations while maintaining or improving surface finish.
Better chip evacuation with dynamic motion results from consistent engagement and reduced dwelling in cuts.
Dynamic Contour automatically converts to dynamic motion in areas where standard contour would cause tool binding.
Profile entry method provides controlled low-angle entry into material, reducing shock loads on tool and spindle.
Full-depth cutting with Dynamic Mill extends tool life by maintaining consistent chip load rather than varying with multiple depth passes.
Entry feeds/speeds separate from cut parameters allow optimized entry conditions without compromising main cutting efficiency.
Toolpath stays inside machining region boundary (Stay Inside strategy), eliminating outside-material rapid moves.
Rest Mill strategy targets only unmachined areas, eliminating air cutting over previously machined surfaces.
High stepover percentage (400-500%) for rest milling maximizes engagement with remaining material pockets.
Dynamic motion pattern avoids sharp direction changes that cause tool deflection and chatter at high speeds.
Contour wall parameters help calculate most efficient removal strategy when approaching walls at high speed.
Helix entry with controlled plunge angle provides smooth tool loading for high-speed entry into pockets.
Custom entry chain option allows entry at known air/pre-machined locations for fastest safe engagement.
From Outside strategy provides efficient facing with island avoidance, tool free to move outside boundary for optimal paths.
Dynamic toolpaths are incremental evolution of HST family, combining familiar 2D concepts with intelligent motion patterns.

x8_specific.content: Tool Manager in X8 uses new TOOLDB database format - faster, more reliable, and non-proprietary for manufacturer integration.
Stand-alone Tool Manager can run without Mastercam open (after initial Mastercam launch to build support files).
Renishaw Productivity+ integrated into X8 for probing operations. Requires Mill Level 1 minimum.
Model Prep functions in X8 allow modification of imported brick solids without history tree access.
Dynamic Mill X8 supports three machining strategies: Stay Inside, From Outside, and Rest Material.
X8 configuration files: mcamxm.config for Metric, mcamx.config for English. Load via Settings > Configuration.
X8 file format is MCX-8 (full version) or EMCX-8 (Demo/HLE - limited functionality, cannot post).
Productivity+ in X8 supports 3-axis, 4-axis, and multiaxis (3+2) mills but not continuous 4/5-axis probing.
X8 Solids features dynamic preview showing results as parameters are edited before finalizing operations.
Tool Manager X8 auto-saves work as you edit, eliminating manual backup requirements during tool library management.
X8 Planes page in toolpath dialog includes 'Display relative to WCS' option for clearer plane relationship understanding.
Chain Options dialog in X8 Dynamic Mill provides dedicated Select buttons for Machining, Avoidance, Containment, and Air regions.
